lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The résumé includes a birth date and nationality.
items.because: Readers do not need those details to assess your qualifications.

items.says: Education leads the résumé instead of relevant experience and projects.
items.because: Opening with education delays the career information a reader is likely to look for first.

items.says: The flow change does not establish a 35% conversion lift for all merchants.
items.because: Without a measurement and comparison, the lift and its scope are unclear.

items.says: The 35% figure does not specify relative growth or a percentage-point change.
items.because: Without a starting rate or type of change, readers cannot judge the improvement’s scale.

items.says: The early-shipment result is buried after the deliverables and stakeholder list.
items.because: A scanning reader reaches the outcome only after the requirements and coordination.

items.says: Six months of data do not by themselves establish annual losses of 1.1 million dollars.
items.because: The line does not show the calculation or assumptions behind the annual figure.

items.says: The roadmap impact comes after a lengthy list of methods and the loss estimate.
items.because: Readers must work through those details before reaching the result.

items.says: The onboarding comparison reports no result.
items.because: Readers learn how merchants were compared but not whether the redesign improved onboarding.

items.says: The bullet credits improved delivery performance to excluding shipments from the calculation.
items.because: Changing which shipments count can lower the reported rate without making deliveries arrive earlier.

items.says: “Prepares” is present tense even though the role ended in August 2023.
items.because: It implies you still prepare the forecast pack in that role.

items.says: The bullet gives no outcome of the review or forecast pack.
items.because: Readers can see the work but not why it mattered.

items.says: “Quarterly” and “for each meeting” redundantly describe the review cadence.
items.because: Both phrases convey how often the review occurs without clarifying the work.

items.says: The claim that the 9 tonnes would otherwise have been thrown away is not established.
items.because: Surplus food might have been eaten or donated another way.

items.says: The launch outcome does not say what product or launch work you personally led.
items.because: Readers can see the app’s outcome but not your contribution behind it.

items.says: The user-interview rationale comes before the main result.
items.because: A scanning reader may not reach the weekly-active-user growth figure quickly.

items.says: The intake-form change gives no measure of how much the form was shortened or what improved.
items.because: Adoption does not show whether intake became faster, simpler or otherwise better.

items.says: The 2,300-merchant onboarding result repeats the Harbor Payments achievement under a hospital-network practicum.
items.because: The entries describe the same merchant result but give different reductions, making it appear misattributed.

items.says: “It takes” uses present tense for a practicum that ended in May 2024.
items.because: The tense makes the result sound current despite the project’s end date.
